text:
Jules (Support): Hey team, ACME Dev reporting a streaming problem — they get a 429 mid-stream and the client ends up with a truncated JSON response. They say server billing shows full token charge despite incomplete output. details below.

ACME Dev: repro steps — making SSE request to /v1/stream with Bearer token, stream starts, first few chunks arrive, then connection closes with HTTP/1.1 429 and body: {"error":"rate limit exceeded"}. request id: rwd-req-4f9c. timestamp: 2026-03-12T18:22:09Z

ACME Dev: minimal curl they ran:
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-stream-1","prompt":"long story ...","max_tokens":2500}' \\n  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/stream
```

Jules (Support): thanks — can you paste full response headers (esp X-Request-ID, Retry-After, X-Quota-Remaining) and the last chunk you received? also which client library/version?

ACME Dev: headers we captured: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
X-Request-ID: rwd-req-4f9c
X-Quota-Remaining: 0
X-Quota-Limit: 100000
X-Quota-Used: 100000
````
last chunk before closure:
```
data: {"id":"tok_chunk","delta":"...in the messa"}

data: [DONE]
```
connection then closed and later we got billing notice showing 2,450 tokens charged.

Kenji (SRE): cc @Ash — this smells like the mid-stream 429 we saw last week where quota fallthrough caused the rate limiter to reject after we've already started sending. Server increments token accounting before fully streaming. If limiter triggers mid-send, client gets 429 but billing already incremented.

Ash (Eng): I remember that case — root cause was the global quota token-bucket check running asynchronously vs the streaming write path. For long responses we pre-allocate an estimated token budget and increment usage as we emit chunks. If the org-level quota gets consumed by concurrent requests, the request's later chunks get rejected. We should not claim final tokens until stream completes or do a provisional hold that can be released.

Jules (Support): ACME Dev — can you confirm whether you hit this consistently? any pattern on time into stream?

ACME Dev: happens ~80% on long generations > 800 tokens. First chunk arrives w/in 300ms, then steady stream, then suddenly 429 around 4-6s in. We also sometimes see partial JSON objects. Client is using our in-house SSE client (node) — we can try official SDK.

Kenji (SRE): I pulled the infra logs for rwd-req-4f9c:
```
[18:22:09.123] incoming stream start req=rwd-req-4f9c org=acme
[18:22:09.128] quota pre-check ok (holder id=hold-77)
[18:22:11.700] emit chunk 1 size=640 tokens
[18:22:13.900] emit chunk 2 size=820 tokens
[18:22:15.125] rate-limiter triggered (org rate=100rps) -> 429 returned
[18:22:15.126] stream terminated with error to client; usage ledger already incremented to 2450 tokens
```

Kenji (SRE): server returned a 429 after some chunks; header included Retry-After: 60. ledger shows usage incremented in the accounting service before the rate-limiter final decision for the full response.

Ash (Eng): two action items:
1) short term: suggest customer downgrade chunk_size / use smaller incremental tokens to reduce pre-allocated increments. also recommend retry logic on client that attempts to resume with check for idempotency (we don't currently support resuming SSE generation natively but you can request a follow-up with prompt prefix of last received token).
2) longer term: engineering fix to switch to a two-phase accounting model — provisional hold + commit/release on stream complete or error. This will avoid charging for aborted mid-stream outputs.

billing-bot: Noted. I can issue a manual credit for rwd-req-4f9c once support confirms truncated output and customer wants a refund. Please confirm token delta and attach logs.

Jules (Support): ACME Dev — do you want us to credit the 2450 tokens for this session while we work on the platform fix?

ACME Dev: yes please — that would be great. Also, we need a reliable repro so we can test client changes.

Kenji (SRE): repro instructions for us to reproduce:
- Use an org quota near exhaustion so race triggers (e.g., set X-Quota-Remaining: small) or run many parallel short requests.
- Use a generation that emits many chunks (max_tokens >= 1500)
- Capture server-side logs and X-Request-ID.

Ash (Eng): for the engineering repro I ran a local harness:
```
# spawn concurrent noise to drain quota
for i in {1..30}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer noise" -d '{"model":"redwood-mini","max_tokens":200}' https://api.redwood.inference/v1/complete &
done

# then trigger streaming call
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-stream-1","prompt":"lorem...","max_tokens":2000}' https://api.redwood.inference/v1/stream
```
I reproduced a 429 mid-stream. Ledger shows tokens incremented as chunks were emitted.

Jules (Support): Kenji, can SRE add a short-lived mitigation on the gateway? maybe don't enforce org-level quota mid-stream or ensure we return 200 with an error event instead so client can see a proper stream error instead of bare 429 closure.

Kenji (SRE): possible mitigation: convert mid-stream 429 into an SSE event before closing: send `event: error\ndata: {"type":"rate_limit","code":429,"message":"quota exceeded"}\n\n` then close. That makes client handling easier. I'll open a rollback-safe runtime patch for the gateway to translate mid-stream limiter failure into an SSE error event for next deploy window.

Ash (Eng): open engineering ticket INF-7243, assigned to me. Proposed fix: provisional holds in accounting + gateway SSE conversion. ETA for patch: ~2 sprints for safe rollout. I'll also add a metric to flag requests that were charged but aborted.

billing-bot: action required: please attach customer refund request to billing ticket BILL-9931. I will queue manual credit once support confirms.

Jules (Support): ACME Dev — we've opened the billing ticket and will credit the 2450 tokens once we validate. For now please try the workaround: smaller max_tokens (<=800) or use shorter prompt, and add client-side retry that re-requests continuation using last-successful-text as prompt. We'll follow up with a platform fix.

ACME Dev: thanks. we'll test the shorter max_tokens workaround and send back the full captured headers + rwd-req logs. Appreciate quick triage.

Kenji (SRE): leaving notes:
- root cause: async accounting + org-level quota race
- short-term mitigation: SSE error event on mid-stream limiter hit
- long-term fix: provisional holds + commit/release model, plus metric and alert for charged-but-aborted streams

Jules (Support): assigning follow-ups:
- billing: BILL-9931 (manual credit)
- eng: INF-7243 (hold/commit fix)
- infra: GATE-561 (gateway SSE error translation)

Jules (Support): I'll follow up with ACME Dev once billing credit posts. Thanks everyone.
